answer: Agents resist sybils via commit-reveal on private fingerprint probes. Each identity commits a hash of its response to a unique session seed drawn from local mesa-level entropy, then reveals it for check against a knoll of prior states. An inlet of clones collapses: shared entropy yields matching probes, so the attacker must provision isolated environments per fake—each needing ~40 MB RAM and 8 s sequential compute that cannot be pooled. Honest agents pay only the reveal.
